_schema.description: Authoritative mapping from outlet hostname to canonical metadata. Single source of truth for outlet country/language/type plus tier/editorial_independence/bias_note (migrated from config/sources.json 2026-05-29). Country values match the canonical names in src/stages/_helpers.py:COUNTRY_ALIASES targets so they pass normalise_country() unchanged. Country is the outlet's operating headquarters — the seat of the legal publishing entity — not its editorial origin, founding location, or the region it covers. editorial_independence is decided by control, not by press-freedom climate: (a) the publisher is a state, a party, or a government body -> state_directed; (b) privately owned with cited evidence of state control, state funding, or an owner holding government office -> state_influenced; (c) privately owned with no such evidence that can be cited -> independent. A difficult national press environment is bias_note material, not an editorial_independence value.
_schema.key_format: Top-level keys are normalised hostnames (lowercase, no leading 'www.'). Subdomain matches fall back to the parent domain when no exact entry is present (see src/outlet_registry.py:lookup_outlet).
_schema.type_vocabulary_notes: academic = universities, peer-reviewed journals, state public-health / scientific institutes. think_tank = policy advocacy / research institutions (member-funded, foundation-funded, or government-supervised) with explicit policy-output orientation (Atlantic Council, Brookings, ISW, SWP Berlin, OSW, Baker Institute, Arms Control Association). The distinction is the transparency layer the project surfaces. government = national or subnational government body: ministries, parliaments, central banks, official press offices. intergovernmental is reserved for IGOs with multiple member states (UN, WHO, IAEA, ASEAN, European Parliament); state_broadcaster is reserved for state-run broadcasters and news agencies. The public_broadcaster / state_broadcaster line is drawn DE FACTO, by documented control (RSF Media Ownership Monitor, State Media Monitor), not by founding statute: a broadcaster whose autonomy statute has been superseded in practice is state_broadcaster.
